ἀκούω.long: I hear, listen, comprehend by hearing; pass: is heard, reported.
ἀκούω.kj: give (in the) audience (of), come (to the ears), (shall) hear(-er, -ken), be noised, be reported, understand
ἀκούω.as:
ἀκούω,
[in LXX chiefly for שׁמע;]
to hear, listen, attend, perceive by hearing, comprehend by hearing.
1. Intrans.: Mk 4:37:37, Ja 2:5, Re 2:7, al.; τ. ὠσίν, Mt 13:15(LXX); c. cogn. dat., ακοῇ ἀ. (v.s. ἀκοή), Mt 13:14, Ac 28:26(LXX); ὁ ἔχων ὦτα (οὖς) ἀκούειν, ἀκουσάτω, Mt 11:15, Mk 4:23, Re 2:7, al.
2. Trans., prop. c. acc. rei, of thing heard, gen. pers., from whom heard (LS, s.v.): Ac 1:4; c. acc. rei, Mt 12:19, Jo 3:8 (Abbott, JG, 76), Ac 22:9, al.; c. dupl. acc., Jo 12:18, I Co 11:18; c. gen. rei, Jo 7:40 (Abbott, JV, 116); τ. φωνῆς (cf. Heb. שָׁמַע בְּקֹול, Ex 18:19), Jo 5:25, 28Ac 9:7 (on the distinction bet. this and ἀ. φωνήν, ib. 4, v. M, Pr., 66; Field, Notes, 117; Abbott, Essays, 93f.); of God answering prayer, Jo 9:31, I Jo 5:14, 15; c. acc. rei, seq. παρά, Jo 8:26, 40Ac 10:22, II Ti 2:2; id. seq. ἀπό, I Jo 1:5; c. gen. pars. seq. ptcp., Mk 14:58, Lk 18:36, al. (On NT usage generally, v. Bl., §36, 5; Cremer, 82.)

ἀκριβόω.long: I learn carefully, inquire with exactness.
ἀκριβόω.as:
** ἀκριβόω, -ῶ
(< ἀκριβής), [in Aq.: Is 30:849:16*;]
to enquire with exactness, learn carefully: Mt 2:7, 16 (for similar ex., v. MM, VGT, sv.).†

ἀκριβῶς.der: adverb from the same as G196 (ἀκριβέστατος);
ἀκριβῶς.as:
ἀκριβῶς
adv.
(< ἀκριβής), [in LXX: De 19:18 (יָטַב), Da TH 7:19 (יְצֵב), Ez 39:14, Wi 19:18, Si 18:29;]
with exactness, carefully: Mt 2:8, Lk 1:3, Ac 18:25, Eph 5:15, I Th 5:2 (M, Th., in l.). Compar., ἀκριβέστερον (Milligan, NTD, 111; MM, VGT, s.v.), Ac 18:2623:15, 2024:22.†

ἀκρίς.sd: a locust (as pointed, or as lighting on the top of vegetation)
ἀκρίς.der: apparently from the same as G206 (ἄκρον);
ἀκρίς.as:
ἀκρίς, -ίδος, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for אַרְבֶּה, also for חָגָב, etc.;]
a locust: Mt 3:4, Mk 1:6, Re 9:3, 7.†

ἀκολουθέω.sd: properly, to be in the same way with, i.e. to accompany (specially, as a disciple)
ἀκολουθέω.der: from G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) and (a road);
ἀκολουθέω.as:
ἀκολουθέω, -ῶ
(< ἀκόλουθος, following; < ἀ- cop., κέλευθος, poët., away), [in LXX chiefly for הָלַךְ;]
to accompany, follow: Mt 4:25, al. Metaph., of discipleship: Mt 9:9, Mk 9:38, Jo 12:26, al. Absol.: Mt 18:10; more freq., c. dat. (cl.), Mt 8:1, al.; seq. μετά, c. gen, (cl.; Eutherford, N.Phr., 458 f.), Lk 9:49; ὀπίσω, c. gen. (Heb. הָלַךְ אחֲֲרֵי), Mt 10:38 (cf. ἐξ-, ἐπ-, κατ-, παρ-, συν-ἀκολουθέω).
SYN.: (cl.) ἕπομαι, not in NT (v. Cremer, 80; MM, VGT, s.v.).

ἀκοή.long: hearing, faculty of hearing, ear; report, rumor.
ἀκοή.sd: hearing (the act, the sense or the thing heard)
ἀκοή.kj: audience, ear, fame, which ye heard, hearing, preached, report, rumor
ἀκοή.as:
ἀκοή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< ἀκούω), [in LXX: Ex 15:26, al. for שׁמע, its parts and derivatives, exc. De 11:22 (שׁמר);]
1.hearing, the sense of hearing: I Co 12:17, II Pe 2:8; "Hebraic dative," ἀκοῇ ακούειν (freq. in LXX; V. M, Pr., 14, 75), Mt 13:14, Ac 28:26.
2.organ of hearing, the ear (Arist., al.; MM, VGT, s.v.): II Ti 4:3, 4; pl., Mk 7:35, Lk 7:1, Ac 17:20, He 5:11.
3.a thing heard, i.e.,
(a)a message, teaching: Jo 12:38 and Ro 16:16, 17(LXX), Ga 3:2, 5 R, mg.; λόγος ἀκοῆς, I Th 2:13, He 4:2;
(b)a report, rumour: c. gen, pers., Mt 4:24, 14:1, 24:6; Mk 1:2813:7 (Cremer, 82, 623; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἄκανθα.long: a thorn-bush, prickly plant; a thorn.
ἄκανθα.der: probably from the same as G188 (ἀκμήν);
ἄκανθα.as:
ἄκανθα, -ης, ἡ
(< ἀκή, a point), [in LXX chiefly for קוֹץ, also for סִיר, שַׁיִת, etc.;]
a prickly plant, thorn, brier; in NT always pl.: Mt 7:1613:7, 2227:29, Mk 4:7, 18, Lk 6:448:7, 14, Jo 19:2, He 6:8 (v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀκάθαρτος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G2508 (καθαίρω) (meaning cleansed);
ἀκάθαρτος.as:
ἀκάθαρτος, -ον
(< ἀ- neg., καθαίρω), [in LXX chiefly for טָמֵא;]
unclean, impure;
(a) physically (LS, MM, VGT, s.v.);
(b) ceremonially: Ac 10:14, 2811:8, I Co 7:14, II Co 6:17, Re 18:2;
(c) morally: Eph 5:5, Re 17:4; c. πνεῦμα, as always in Gosp., Mt 10:112:43, Mk 1:23, 26, 273:11, 305:2, 8, 136:77:259:25, Lk 4:33, 366:188:299:4211:24, Ac 5:168:7, Re 16:13 (cf. Cremer, 320).†

ἀκέραιος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G2767 (κεράννυμι);
ἀκέραιος.as:
** ἀκέραιος, -ον
(< κεράννυμι), [in LXX: Es 8:13*;]
unmixed, pure, hence, metaph. (cf. MM, VGT, s.v.), guileless, simple: Mt 10:16, Ro 16:19, Phl 2:15.†
SYN.: ἄδολος, ἄκακος, ἁπλοῦς (cf. Ellic. on Phl 2:15; Tr., Syn., §lvi).

ἄκαρπος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2590 (καρπός);
ἄκαρπος.as:
ἄ-καρπος, -ον,
[in LXX: Je 2:6 (צַלְמָוֶת), Wi 15:4, IV Mac 16:7;]
unfruitful, barren: fig., Mt 13:22, Mk 4:19, I Co 14:14, Eph 5:11, Tit 3:14, II Pe 1:8, Ju 12.†

ἀκυρόω.g: I annul, make of no effect, cancel
ἀκυρόω.long: I annul, make of no effect, cancel.
ἀκυρόω.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2964 (κυρόω);
ἀκυρόω.as:
**† ἀκυρόω, -ῶ
(< κῦρος, authority), [in LXX: I Es 6:32, IV Mac6*;]
to revoke, invalidate (MM, VGT, s.v.): Mt 15:6, Mk 7:13, Ga 3:17 (Plut.).†

ἀκμήν.der: accusative case of a noun ("acme") akin to (a point) and meaning the same;
ἀκμήν.as:
* ἀκμήν, acc. of ἀκμή,
a point, used as adv., at the present point of time, even now, even yet: Mt 15:16.†

ἀκρασία.long: incontinence, intemperance (in wide sense), lack of restraint.
ἀκρασία.as:
** ἀκρασία, -ας, ἡ
(< ἀκρατής, q.v.), [in LXX: I Mac 6:26*;]
in Arist. and later writers = ἀκράτεια (Lft., Notes, 222 f.), want of power, hence want of self-control, incontinence: Mt 23:25, I Co 7:5.†

ἀκαθαρσία.as:
ἀκαθαρσία, -ας, ἡ
(< ἀκάθαρτος), [in LXX chiefly for טֻמְאָה, טָמֵא;]
uncleanness, impurity,
(a) physical (MM, VGT, s.v.): Mt 23:27;
(b) moral: Ro 1:246:19, II Co 12:21, Ga 5:19, Eph 4:195:3, Col 3:5, I Th 2:34:7.†

ἄκρον.kj: one end… other, tip, top, uttermost participle
ἄκρον.der: neuter of an adjective probably akin to the base of G188 (ἀκμήν);

ἀκάνθινος.as:
ἀκάνθινος, -ον
(< ἄκανθα), [in LXX: Is 34:13 (סיר)*;]
1.of thorns: Mk 15:17, Jo 19:5.
2.of acantha-wood (Hdt.; π. ap. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀκαταστασία.long: disturbance, upheaval, revolution, almost anarchy, first in the political, and thence in the moral sphere.
ἀκαταστασία.as:
† ἀκαταστασία, -ας, ἡ (< ἀκατάστατος),
[in LXX: Pr 26:28 (מִדְחֶה), To 4:13*;]
instability (MM, VGT, s.v.); hence, confusion, tumult: I Co 14:33, Ja 3:16; pl. (Bl., §32, 6), Lk 21:9, II Co 6:5, 12:20 (Polyb., al.; v. Cremer, 739).†

Ἁκελδαμάχ.sd: corresponding to H02506 and H01818); Akeldama, a place near Jerusalem
Ἁκελδαμάχ.der: of Chaldee origin (meaning field of blood;

ἀκροβυστία.long: (a technical word of Jewish use) foreskin, prepuce: used sometimes as a slang term by Jews, of Gentiles.
ἀκροβυστία.sd: the prepuce; by implication, an uncircumcised (i.e. gentile, figuratively, unregenerate) state or person
ἀκροβυστία.der: from G206 (ἄκρον) and probably a modified form of (the penis or male sexual organ);
ἀκροβυστία.as:
† ἀκροβυστία, -ας, ή
(perh. an Alexandrian form of cl. ἀκροποσθία; cf. MM, VGT, s.v.) [in LXX for עׇרְלָה;]
the prepuce, foreskin (LXX), hence abstr., uncircumcision: Ac 11:3, Ro 2:25-273:304:10-12, I Co 7:18-19, Ga 5:66:15, Col 2:133:11. By meton., the uncircumcised: Ro 4:9, Ga 2:7, Eph 2:11.†

ἀκατάκριτος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2632 (κατακρίνω);
ἀκατάκριτος.as:
*† ἀ-κατά-κριτος, -ον
(< κατακρίνω),
1.uncondemned (EV): Ac 16:37, 22:25.
2. = cl. ἄκριτος, without trial, not yet tried (MM, VGT, s.v.) Ac 16:37, 22:25†

Ἀκύλας.long: the Greek way of writing the Latin Aquila, a male proper name; the husband of Priscilla (Prisca), and a Jew, of a family belonging to (Sinope in ?) Pontus.
Ἀκύλας.as:
Ἀκύλας, -ου (and -α; MM, VGT, s.v.), ὁ (Lat.),
Aquila: Ac 18:2, 1818:26, Ro 16:3, I Co 16:19, II Ti 4:19.†

ἀκριβέστερον.der: neuter of the comparative of the same as G196 (ἀκριβέστατος);

ἀκρίβεια.long: strictness, accuracy, exactness, attention to detail, scrupulousness.
ἀκρίβεια.as:
ἀκρίβεια, -ας, ἡ
(< ἀκριβής), [in LXX: Da LXX TH 7:16 (יַצִּיב), Wi 12:21, Si 16:2542:4*;]
exactness, precision (for exx., v. MM, VGT, s.v.): Ac 22:3.†

ἀκροατήριον.long: auditorium, recitation hall, court room (for hearing cases).
ἀκροατήριον.as:
*† ἀκροατήριον, -ου, τό
(< ἀκροάομαι, to listen)
a place of audience: Ac 25:23 (Plut.).†

ἀκριβής.der: superlative of (a derivative of the same as G206 (ἄκρον));
ἀκριβής.as:
ἀκριβής, -ές
[in LXX: Da LXX 2:456:12 (יַצִּיב) Da 4:25, Es 4:5, Si 18:2919:2531:2432:3*;]
exact, precise, careful, of things and persons: superl., Ac 26:5.†

ἀκωλύτως.long: (characteristic of legal documents), without hindrance, freely.
ἀκωλύτως.sd: in an unhindered manner, i.e. freely
ἀκωλύτως.der: adverb from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2967 (κωλύω);
ἀκωλύτως.as:
** ἀκωλύτως
adv.
(< κωλύω), [in Sm.: Jb 34:31*;]
without hindrance (so freq. in legal documents; MM, VGT, s.v.): Ac 28:31.†

ἀκροατής.g: a hearer of, a listener to
ἀκροατής.long: a hearer of, a listener to.
ἀκροατής.sd: apparently an intensive of G191 (ἀκούω)); a hearer (merely)
ἀκροατής.as:
ἀκροατής, οῦ, ὁ (v. supr.)
[in LXX: Is 3:3 (לַחַשׁ), Si 3:29 ;]
a hearer: Ro 2:13, Ja 1:22, 23, 25.†

ἄκακος.sd: not bad, i.e. (objectively) innocent or (subjectively) unsuspecting
ἄκακος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2556 (κακός);
ἄκακος.as:
ἄ-κακος, -ον,
[in LXX for פְּתִי, תָּם, etc.;]
(a) as in cl. (Æsch., Plat., al.), of persons, simple, guileless: Ro 16:18, He 7:26 (cf. Cremer, 327);
(b) of things, undamaged (? MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἄκων.long: unwilling, generally used where English would express by an adverb: unwillingly.
ἄκων.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1635 (ἑκών);
ἄκων.as:
ἄκων (Attic contr. for ἀέκων), -ουσα, -ον
(< ἀ- neg., ἕκων, willing), [in LXX: Jb 14:17, II Mac 11:12*;]
unwilling: I Co 9:17.†

ἀκατακάλυπτος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of G2596 (κατά) and G2572 (καλύπτω);
ἀκατακάλυπτος.as:
† ἀ-κατα-κάλυπτος, -ον
(< κατακαλύπτω), [in LXX: Le 13:45 A (פָּרוּע)*;]
uncovered, unveiled: I Co 11:5, 13.†

ἀκρογωνιαῖος.long: in the corner (of a building); subst: corner-(stone).
ἀκρογωνιαῖος.as:
† ἀκρο-γωνιαῖος, -αία, -αῖον
(< ἄκροι, γωνία, an angle) [in LXX: Is 28:16 (פִּנָּה)*;] = Attic γωνιαῖος (freq. in Inscr.; MM, VGT, s.v. ἀ.),
at the extreme angle: ὁ ἀ., the corner foundation stone, Eph 2:20, I Pe 2:6.†

ἀκαιρέομαι.g: I am without a suitable opportunity
ἀκαιρέομαι.long: I am without a suitable opportunity.
ἀκαιρέομαι.sd: to be inopportune (for oneself), i.e. to fail of a proper occasion
ἀκαιρέομαι.der: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2540 (καιρός) (meaning unseasonable);
ἀκαιρέομαι.as:
*† ἀκαιρέομαι, -οῦμαι
(< ἄκαιρος, unseasonable),
to have no opportunity (opp. to εὐκαιρέω): Phl 4:10.†

ἀκρατής.long: lacking self-control, powerless, inclined to excess.
ἀκρατής.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2904 (κράτος);
ἀκρατής.as:
ἀκρατής, -ές
(< κράτος), [in LXX: Pr 27:20*;]
(a)powerless, impotent;
(b) in moral sense, lacking self-control, incontinent: II Ti 3:3.†

ἀκαίρως.long: unseasonably, out of due season, inopportunely.
ἀκαίρως.der: adverb from the same as G170 (ἀκαιρέομαι);
ἀκαίρως.as:
** ἀκαίρως, adv.
(< ἄκαιρος, unseasonable), [in LXX: Si 35 (32):4*;]
out of season, unseasonably: opp. to εὐκαίρως (q.v.), II Ti 4:2 (cf. Cremer, 740; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀκατάγνωστος.long: not open to just rebuke; irreprehensible.
ἀκατάγνωστος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2607 (καταγινώσκω);
ἀκατάγνωστος.as:
**† ἀ-κατά-γνωστος, -ον
(< καταγινώσκω), [in LXX: II Mac 4:47 ;]
not open to just rebuke, irreprehensible: Tit 2:8 (v. Cremer, 676; and for other exx., MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀκροθίνιον.long: (lit: top of a heap), first-fruits, spoil, treasure (taken in war).
ἀκροθίνιον.sd: properly (in the plural) the top of the heap, i.e. (by implication) best of the booty
ἀκροθίνιον.as:
* ἀκροθίνιον, -ου, τό
(< ἄκρος, θίς, a heap),
prop., the top of a heap, hence, in pl.,
1.first-fruits (Xen.; MM, VGT, s.v.).
2. In war, the choicest spoils (cf. Hdt., viii, 121 f.): He 7:4.†

ἀκατάλυτος.g: indissoluble, that cannot be broken up
ἀκατάλυτος.long: indissoluble, that cannot be broken up.
ἀκατάλυτος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2647 (καταλύω);
ἀκατάλυτος.as:
**† ἀ-κατά-λυτος, -ον
(< καταλύω), [in LXX: IV Mac 10:11*;]
indissoluble: He 7:16.†

ἀκλινής.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2827 (κλίνω);
ἀκλινής.as:
** ἀκλινής, -ές
(< κλίνω), [in LXX: IV Mac 6:717:3*;]
unbending, firm: metaph. (MM, VGT, s.v.). He 10:23.†

ἀκατάστατος.long: unsettled, unstable (though these are hardly strong enough equivalents), almost anarchic.
ἀκατάστατος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2525 (καθίστημι);
ἀκατάστατος.as:
ἀ-κατά-στατος, -ον
(< καθίστημι), [in LXX: Is 54:11 (סֹעֲרָה);]
unsettled, unstable: Ja 1:8, 3:8.†

ἀκατάπαυστος.long: not ceasing from, not abandoning (giving up).
ἀκατάπαυστος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2664 (καταπαύω);
ἀκατάπαυστος.as:
*† ἀκατάπαυστος, -ον
(< καταπαύω),
that cannot cease, not to be restrained: c. gen. rei, II Pe 2:14, T, Tr. txt.†

ἄκρατος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G2767 (κεράννυμι);
ἄκρατος.as:
ἄκρατος, -ον
(< κεράννυμι), [in LXX: Ps 75:8 (חֲמַר), Je 25:15 (חֵמָה), III Mac 5:2*;]
unmixed, pure: οἶνος, Re 14:10.†

ἀκμάζω.long: I reach maturity, become ripe, am in full vigor.
ἀκμάζω.sd: to make a point, i.e. (figuratively) mature
ἀκμάζω.as:
** ἀκμάζω
(< ἀκμήν), [in LXX: IV Mac 2:3*;]
to be at the prime; of produce of the ground, to be ripe (Thuc.): Re 14:18 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†
